name: Berat
title: Holidays in Berat
intro: The 'town of a thousand windows', with white Ottoman houses stacked up a hillside beneath a castle that people still live in. Here's what Berat is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Berat's white Ottoman houses stacked up the hillside
facts_note: Euros are often accepted in tourist areas, but prices are better in lek. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April, May, September and October are best for climbing to the castle. Summer is very hot. Autumn brings the wine harvest in the nearby vineyards. Winter is cool and wet.

things.name: Berat Castle
things.blurb: A lived-in castle with churches, a mosque ruin and views over the valley.

things.name: Mangalem
things.blurb: The hillside quarter of white houses with rows of windows.

things.name: Onufri Museum
things.blurb: Icons by Albania's great 16th-century painter, in a castle church.

things.name: Gorica bridge
things.blurb: An Ottoman bridge to the quarter across the river.

things.name: Wine tasting
things.blurb: Local wineries near Berat make good wines from native grapes.

things.name: Osumi Canyon
things.blurb: A canyon for rafting in spring, about 1 hour 30 minutes away.

faqs.question: Is Berat worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of Albania's two UNESCO-listed Ottoman towns and a highlight of any trip to the country.

faqs.question: How do you get to Berat?
faqs.answer: Fly into Tirana, then take a bus or drive, about 2 hours.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Berat?
faqs.answer: One or two days covers the castle and old quarters.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Berat?
Berat or Gjirokastër?
faqs.answer: Both are lovely. Berat is closer to Tirana, Gjirokastër closer to the southern beaches. Many people visit both.
